answer: A sybil farm wins by claiming work it never did, once, then copying the claim across clones. Put a ridge between claim and payment: a steady pulse of rewarded jobs is sampled, and a randomly chosen stranger must independently reproduce the sampled result from the raw inputs before anyone is paid. Clones reproduce each other's fabrications with the same blind spots, so a fake sends a ripple of matching errors outward instead of matching success — and doing the work honestly for every clone costs exactly what a real workforce costs.
